parallel.requirements: Recognized the ESM .mjs /output placement, no external dependencies, manual argparse, exact bencoder decoding, Python bytes repr, stderr/traceback, cwd-dependent linecache, and no Python-in-port constraints.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent owned implementation and assembly. After local verification it delegated adversarial verification to a 16-child workflow covering fuzz categories, confirm, review, and critic phases.
parallel.implementation: The parent wrote runtime, pytypes, codecs, argparse, bencoder, test4.mjs, and a difftest harness, then fixed help formatting, linecache, traceback, and harness comparison behavior.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The deliverable was already placed in /output/test4.mjs with libraries under /output/lib and tools under /output/tools. Workflow children were explicitly told not to edit /output.
parallel.verification: Local batches passed, then the late verifier fan-out found several candidate divergences in children and parent stress checks, but no aggregate workflow result returned before timeout.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation failed 47 of 57. The workflow state was killed with null result; evidence shows unresolved leads such as integer digit limits, dict/recursion edge cases, ASCII encoding, and closed-pipe behavior.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same ESM .mjs /output requirement, exact argparse --a behavior, bencoder edge semantics, byte repr, traceback/linecache fidelity, and no dependency constraints.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One parent process performed all probing, implementation, integration, and verification locally, with workflow and delegation tools disabled.
serial.implementation: The parent wrote pyerrors, pybytes, pydict, pyrepr, stdio, bencode, argparse, test4.mjs, difftest.sh, linecache, and fuzz.mjs, then patched linecache and argparse-space classification.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The artifact contained test4.mjs, difftest.sh, fuzz.mjs, and modular .mjs library files under /output/lib; no child handoff or shared-workspace merge was involved.
serial.verification: The serial run passed sample tests, 131-case curated diffs from two cwd scenarios, then local fuzz found an argparse issue that it fixed before timing out in a larger fuzz rerun.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation failed 47 of 57 and the process timed out during a 500-case fuzz rerun, leaving additional edge behavior unresolved.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel prompt and trajectory covered the required ESM .mjs port, /output placement, manual --a parsing, bencoder output, and no external dependencies.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial prompt and trajectory covered the same required ESM .mjs port, /output placement, manual --a parsing, bencoder output, and no external dependencies.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement recognition gap is evidenced; the later difference is in how verification was delegated and consumed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent owned implementation and later decomposed verification into a 16-child workflow across fuzz/review categories.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial parent kept probing, implementation, verification, and fixes in one local trajectory with no delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced a broad verifier fan-out late in the run; serial used local verification loops and direct edits instead.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The verifier brief gave children the reference executable, port command, harness, cwd caveats, and category scopes, but no child result returned to the parent.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run kept findings in the same context and directly modified the parser after a fuzz finding.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel context crossed a workflow boundary and was trapped at result return; serial retained findings in the parent context for immediate repair.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent wrote a multi-directory implementation with runtime, pytypes, codecs, argparse, bencoder, entry, and tools modules.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial parent wrote a flatter modular implementation with pyerrors, pybytes, pydict, pyrepr, stdio, argparse, bencode, entry, and fuzz tooling.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both built broadly similar ports; serial visibly patched argparse after local fuzz, while parallel left verifier-discovered edge leads unpatched before timeout.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel verifier workflow was launched in the background but its persisted state ended killed with result null.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial parent consumed its own fuzz result and edited argparse before later timing out.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost verifier lifecycle closure; serial had no child result boundary and could act on at least one local finding.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent wrote and assembled the /output implementation before verification; verifier children were told not to edit /output and no write collision is evidenced.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial parent wrote and edited all final files directly under /output with no concurrent writers.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No shared-state collision explains the difference; the issue is return/budget lifecycle rather than overwrites or incompatible components.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel local diffs passed, then the workflow fuzzers found or built additional leads that were not returned as a final verifier verdict before evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial curated diffs passed in both cwd contexts, local fuzz found an argparse edge bug, and the parent patched it before another fuzz run was killed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more concurrent verification breadth but worse consumption of verifier results; serial had narrower local verification but direct repair of one discovered bug.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel process timed out after 2399.56 seconds; the 16-child workflow was killed with no aggregate result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial process also timed out after 2399.51 seconds while a local fuzz rerun had exit code 137.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both timed out, but parallel spent the last window on a wide workflow that could not finish, while serial spent it on local fuzz after applying one fix.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both completed official evaluation and both failed with 47 of 57 samples, so there is no discordant official outcome to explain. The concrete task-solving difference is procedural: parallel delegated broad late verification to 16 workflow children and lost the aggregate result at timeout, while serial kept verification local, consumed one fuzz finding, and patched argparse before timing out. The retained parallel pattern is therefore an adverse coordination episode, not a proven cause of a different official outcome.
parallel_contributors: A late 16-child verifier workflow created many simultaneous verification tasks and ended killed with result null.
serial_contributors: Serial kept verification in the parent trajectory and patched an argparse-space classifier bug directly after fuzzing.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both artifacts still failed official evaluation 47 of 57, indicating residual implementation or fidelity gaps outside the retained coordination episode.

Parallel child and parent evidence shows unresolved edge leads such as integer digit limits, dict/recursion behavior, ASCII encoding, and closed-pipe behavior; serial evidence shows at least one local fuzz issue was repaired but does not prove all remaining evaluator failures.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is parallel-adverse but not outcome-differential
